articles.title: 'Stabbed 7 times with dagger': How bid to seal petrol pump turned deadly for IndianOil official
articles.summary: CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: An IndianOil sales manager died after being stabbed seven times with a dagger while on duty in Hingoli district on Tuesday.
articles.body: CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: An IndianOil sales manager died after being stabbed seven times with a dagger while on duty in Hingoli district on Tuesday. Within 24 hours, police arrested all five accused.On Tuesday morning, Mahesh Shelke (37) had gone to a petrol pump as part of a team to seal and take over the outlet. Hours later, the engineer was dead. What began as negotiations over handing over the outlet at Chondhi village in Vasmat taluka spiralled into a violent confrontation. Shelke was allegedly attacked with a dagger while others pelted stones at him, police said. Shelke was manager (retail sales) with Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL)’s Nanded office.How it all unfoldedOn Tuesday, Shelke was among the IOC officials and employees who reached the petrol pump around noon to seal it and take possession following a dispute with the Pandavveer family, which operated the outlet.Talks went on for hours. The family reportedly sought a month’s time and assured officials it would allow IOC to take over the outlet thereafter. But the company team remained firm on sealing the pump. The stand-off then turned violent.Hingoli SP Shrenik Lodha said preliminary probe showed that Umesh Pandavveer allegedly attacked Shelke with a dagger during the altercation. He allegedly stabbed Shelke seven times. Some of the other accused allegedly pelted stones, creating panic at the spot.Shelke suffered grievous injuries. A Kurunda police team led by assistant police inspector Shivaji Puri reached the spot and Shelke was taken to hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead.Five arrested within 24 hoursPolice registered an FIR on the complaint of IndianOil senior manager Gullakantla Maniprasad. They booked five people for murder, attempt to murder, unlawful assembly and rioting, besides invoking provisions of the Arms Act.Lodha said all five were arrested within 24 hours. Police identified them as Latabai Pandavveer (46), her son Umesh (25), and their acquaintances Shravan Wakude (21), Rahul Dhayje (37) and Prathmesh Waghmare (27).Shelke’s body was taken to Vasmat sub-district hospital for autopsy before being handed over to his family.Who was Mahesh Shelke?Shelke was manager (retail sales) with Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL)’s Nanded office. A mechanical engineering graduate from an engineering college in Pune, he hailed from a village in Ahmedpur taluka of Latur district.He joined IndianOil in 2014 and served in south India before being transferred to Maharashtra in 2024. For the past two years, he had been living with his family in Nanded district.‘Heinous, unacceptable’: Puri on IOCL sales manager’s murderThe killing of an official while on duty drew sharp reactions from Union petroleum and natural gas minister Hardeep Singh Puri, who took up the matter with Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and DGP Sadanand Date.“The issue (stabbing of Shelke) has been taken up with the senior-most officials of the Maharashtra govt and police to ensure swift and strict action against those responsible, in accordance with law,” Puri said in a post on X.Calling it a “heinous and unacceptable act of violence”, Puri said the petroleum ministry and IndianOil would extend all possible support to Shelke’s family.IndianOil seeks ‘swift and stringent action’IndianOil chairman A S Sahney told PTI that the company had taken up the case with the “highest authorities in Maharashtra”, seeking “swift and stringent action”.“Deeply anguished by the tragic loss of our colleague, Mahesh Shelke, who was fatally attacked while discharging his official duties in Hingoli, Maharashtra,” Sahney said.Stay updated with the latest Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar news. articles.title: This Arizona ranch spans 114,000 acres and has stayed with one family for nearly 80 years; now it is listed for $43 million
articles.summary: A sprawling stretch of the Sonoran Desert that has remained in the same family for nearly 80 years is now on the market for $43 million.
articles.body: A sprawling stretch of the Sonoran Desert that has remained in the same family for nearly 80 years is now on the market for $43 million. According to Mansion Global, Marley Ranch, located between Tucson and Nogales in southern Arizona, spans more than 114,000 acres within its ranch boundary and is being offered for the first time in more than 75 years. The ranch has been in the Marley family's ownership since Kemper and Ethel Marley established it in the 1940s and later expanded it. It includes rolling grasslands surrounded by high mountains and sits on the west side of the Santa Cruz River, an area associated with the routes of Spanish conquistadors and the missionary Father Kino. The property can accommodate up to 1,600 cattle, although the cattle and ranch equipment are not included in the asking price.A 114,000-acre ranch with 1,600-cattle capacityMarley Ranch spans 114,279.48 acres, equivalent to 178.56 sections, according to the current property listing. However, the entire acreage is not privately owned land. The ranch consists of 17,265.07 acres of deeded land alongside land held through several grazing arrangements, including a large Arizona State Land Department grazing lease, a Bureau of Land Management allotment, private grazing licenses and leases, and Pima County land.The listing says the ranch has a carrying capacity of 1,600 animal units during normal rainfall years, although actual use varies depending on rainfall. Mansion Global similarly reports that the ranch can accommodate up to 1,600 head of cattle. The animals and equipment are separate from the $43 million sale price. The property is built around an extensive cattle operation. It has 28 major pastures, several large working corrals, smaller branding corrals and traps, as well as 60 dirt stock ponds. Its water infrastructure includes 19 stock wells, of which 15 are operating, along with 4 domestic wells and 2 grandfathered irrigation wells. Ten of the ranch's wells are solar-powered. More than 52 miles of pipeline, with storage and troughs, help distribute water across the property.The ranch stretches across 2 Arizona countiesThe Marley Cattle Company is located in southern Arizona's Sonoran Desert, about 20 miles south of Tucson and near Amado. The ranch lies west of Interstate 19, with the headquarters located along Arivaca Road in Santa Cruz County and another homestead area in Pima County. The property is roughly 20 miles wide from east to west and about 15 miles from north to south on its western side, according to the listing. The ranch's elevation ranges from about 3,109 feet above sea level at the homestead to 4,700 feet in the Colorado Mountains, with most of the property between 3,200 and 3,800 feet. The listing describes the ranch as being on the west side of the Santa Cruz River, which it identifies as a historic route associated with Spanish conquistadors and Father Kino.Despite its size, the ranch is equipped for a working cattle operation rather than being simply undeveloped desert acreage. Its headquarters includes a ranch manager's double-wide mobile home, 3 small ranch-hand houses, another mobile home, a shop, hay shed, tack room, covered horse pens, shipping corrals with a scale and a feed yard. At the separate homestead, the listing includes an owner's residence and bunkhouses that are currently non-habitable, along with a guest house and a residence occupied by ranch hands. There is also a dirt airstrip at the homestead that, when maintained, can accommodate twin-engine aircraft. The ranch is fenced around its perimeter, while roads across the property are maintained by the ranch.A Marley family property since the 1940sThe ranch's history stretches back to Kemper and Ethel Marley, who acquired land in the 1940s and expanded the property. According to Mansion Global, the couple made their primary home in Phoenix but were closely involved in ranch life, including riding with crews during cattle roundups. Kemper Marley, who built a business empire that included cattle farms and other companies, died in 1990 at age 83. Ethel Marley died in 1997 at age 90.The ranch remained with the Marley family after their deaths. Mansion Global reports that it was eventually turned over to their 3 nephews, while the current generation did not want to continue owning the property. The current listing describes the ranch as being offered for sale for the first time in more than 75 years, making the $43 million listing a significant change for a property that has remained associated with the Marley family for decades. Mansion Global reported that Marley Ranch is one of the most expensive listings in Arizona and described it as the state's most expensive ranch listing at the time of its March 2026 report. The current listing price remains $43 million, with the cattle and equipment excluded from the sale.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Tulsa’s Arkansas River waterfront sat underused for years; billionaire George Kaiser put $465 million behind a 66-acre park that became a major public destination
articles.summary: The Arkansas River was once a difficult backdrop for Tulsa, with stretches of its waterfront offering little reason for residents to linger.
articles.body: The Arkansas River was once a difficult backdrop for Tulsa, with stretches of its waterfront offering little reason for residents to linger. That changed with the arrival of Gathering Place, a vast public park built with private funding and designed around recreation, culture and open space. Associated Press (AP) reported when it opened, the 66-acre first phase brought playgrounds, trails, sports facilities, lawns and gathering areas to the riverfront. The project was backed by the foundation of billionaire philanthropist George Kaiser, whose contribution helped finance a development that would eventually expand towards 100 acres. What began as an ambitious piece of urban redevelopment has since become one of Tulsa's most visited public spaces.A neglected stretch of the Arkansas River gets a new purposeTulsa's relationship with the Arkansas River has not always been straightforward. The waterway runs through the city, but parts of its banks had long been underused, leaving a large amount of valuable urban space disconnected from everyday life.As reported by AP News, Gathering Place was conceived as a way of changing that. Rather than treating the riverfront simply as somewhere to pass through, the project put public activity at the centre of the design.The first phase covered about 66 acres, with plans for the park to eventually reach roughly 100 acres. The grounds were laid out for different kinds of use, from quiet walks and cycling to organised sport, concerts and family outings. The park was intended to work as a place people could visit for a few hours, but also as a setting for larger civic and cultural events.George Kaiser put private wealth behind a public parkGathering Place was built with private money, with major support coming from the George Kaiser Family Foundation. Kaiser, a Tulsa-born billionaire, had already become one of the city's most prominent philanthropists. His foundation's involvement gave the riverfront project access to a level of private funding rarely available for a conventional municipal park.The result was not simply a landscaped strip beside the river. The money went towards a substantial collection of facilities and public spaces, creating an environment intended to serve residents across different age groups and interests.Playgrounds, trails and courts spread across the siteVisitors arriving at Gathering Place encounter a park built around movement and activity rather than a single central attraction. There are walking and cycling routes, athletic courts and broad lawns that can accommodate concerts and other gatherings. Play areas were also a major part of the design, with children given dedicated spaces to climb, explore and play.The range of facilities means the park can feel different depending on when it is visited. A weekday morning might bring walkers and families, while evenings and weekends can draw larger crowds for performances and events.The river itself remains an important part of the setting. Instead of turning its back on Arkansas, the park incorporates the waterfront into the experience, making the landscape part of the attraction.Gathering Place draws hundreds for its opening day in TulsaWhen Gathering Place opened, hundreds of people gathered along the Tulsa riverfront to mark the occasion. The launch was designed as a public celebration rather than a conventional ribbon-cutting ceremony. A parade opened the day's programme, followed by live music and activities for children.Kaiser joined Oklahoma Gov. Mary Fallin and local officials for the opening, as residents explored a park that had taken years of planning and construction to reach that point. The crowds offered an early indication of how much interest the project had generated. For Tulsa, the opening also represented a significant change in how one of the city's major pieces of open land could be used.The park was designed around inclusion as well as recreationCity leaders described Gathering Place as more than a collection of playgrounds, sports courts and green spaces. The project was also presented as an experiment in creating a public setting where people from different parts of the city could meet. That ambition influenced the range of spaces included in the park. There are areas intended for active recreation, quieter corners, performance spaces and facilities aimed at families.The emphasis on accessibility and broad public use was particularly important because the park had been financed privately. Its purpose was not to create an exclusive development around the river, but a public destination available to people without an admission charge.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: ‘Angry and confused’: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike wakes up after surviving execution attempt
articles.summary: US death-row inmate Christa Pike woke up “angry and confused” in a Tennessee hospital days after surviving a botched lethal injection, her lawyer said on
articles.body: US death-row inmate Christa Pike woke up “angry and confused” in a Tennessee hospital days after surviving a botched lethal injection, her lawyer said on Wednesday.Pike’s first words after regaining consciousness were “Where am I?” and “Who are you?”on Tuesday in what her lawyer described as a “shock to everyone”. Her legal team had believed for days that she was brain dead and expected doctors to withdraw life support.Pike is believed to be the only person to survive an execution attempt by lethal injection.She remembers only limited details of the September 30 execution attempt, during which she was administered two rounds of the drug pentobarbital.“We don't know the toll all of this will take” on her mental health, Spivey said, describing her as “angry and confused” after the ordeal.Judge orders evidence from execution preservedA Tennessee judge on Wednesday ordered the state to preserve all evidence connected to the failed execution after Pike’s lawyers sought an emergency order.The order covers items from the execution room, including IV lines and syringes, as well as packaging, inserts and labels. The judge also ordered the preservation of documentation concerning Pike’s psychological condition before, during and after the execution.Pike’s lawyer Luke Ihnen told the court that communication with his client had been difficult because she had remained unconscious until Tuesday and was now only “speaking limitedly”.The legal team said the preserved evidence could form the basis of a future lawsuit against the state.Could Tennessee try to execute Pike again?Tennessee could attempt to execute Pike again, but any effort to use lethal injection is likely to face significant legal challenges, according to Tennessee-based defence attorney Stephen Ross Johnson, BBC reported.“For the state to attempt to execute her again using the same methodology, they would have severe legal hurdles,” Johnson said.Johnson said Pike’s medical condition, combined with the failed execution, could make it difficult for the state to justify another attempt using lethal injection.Tennessee could also seek to execute Pike using a different method, although that would involve additional legal hurdles and potentially require approval from the governor’s office and state legislature.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pentagon orders US military to gear up for Iran strikes; Trump yet to decide dates
articles.summary: The Pentagon has instructed the US central command (CENTCOM) to complete preparations for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran.
articles.body: The Pentagon has instructed the US central command (CENTCOM) to complete preparations for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran. US President Donald Trump has not made a final decision yet on whether to launch fresh strikes, Axios reported, citing US officials.According to Axios, the preparations could pave the way for a new US military campaign targeting Iranian nuclear facilities, energy infrastructure and other strategic sites. However, the report said no timeline for an attack has been set and the Pentagon's preparations do not amount to a presidential order to begin strikes.The development comes as Washington's diplomatic efforts with Tehran remain deadlocked.Axios reported that negotiations have stalled, while a separate meeting of Trump's senior national-security team at Camp David last week focused on the Iran war and the escalating Saudi-Houthi conflict in Yemen. The meeting was chaired by Vice President JD Vance and included senior US defence, intelligence, diplomatic and economic officials.The timing is also linked to the US midterm elections and elections in Israel. Axios reported that US and Israeli officials are assessing the possibility of renewed operations before the elections, although an Israeli official said the chances of action before the polls are currently low and could rise after them.Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have spoken twice in recent days. If fighting resumes, US and Israeli forces are expected to operate in tandem, while Israeli officials believe Iran could retaliate with ballistic-missile attacks against Israel.Situation in the Middle EastThe Middle East is facing multiple connected fronts, with the US-Iran war now overlapping with renewed fighting in Yemen, direct Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and continuing Israeli operations in Gaza and the wider region.Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces launched a major offensive against the Iran-backed Houthis earlier this week, seeking to retake territory along the Red Sea coast and around the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait.The Houthis have responded with missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia. Three people were killed and dozens wounded in attacks on Abha and Riyadh's King Khalid International airports, according to Saudi authorities cited by Reuters and AP. The Saudi-led coalition subsequently said it had struck more than 80 Houthi targets in Yemen.Israel is also heading towards elections on October 27, with the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack remaining a central issue in the campaign. AP reported that the election is increasingly being framed around responsibility for the security failure and Netanyahu's handling of the wars that followed.You use AI every day. articles.title: JP Morgan CEO Jamie Dimon has a 'suggestion' for companies building datacenters in America: There are a lot of states that would welcome them, if they have ...
articles.summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has a message for companies rushing to build data centres across the US to power the artificial intelligence boom: focus on
articles.body: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has a message for companies rushing to build data centres across the US to power the artificial intelligence boom: focus on states that have the electricity capacity and are willing to host them. Speaking in an interview with Bloomberg TV, Dimon said data centre developers should prioritise locations where local communities support such projects rather than trying to push developments into areas facing opposition. “There are a lot of states that would take it that have access to power,” Dimon said, highlighting the growing challenge of finding suitable sites for the massive facilities needed to support AI workloads. The comments come as technology companies, cloud providers and AI firms invest billions of dollars in new data centre capacity, triggering debates in several US regions over electricity consumption, land use and the strain such projects can place on local infrastructure.AI boom driving infrastructure demandThe rapid buildout of data centres has been fuelled by surging demand for computing power as companies race to develop and deploy increasingly advanced AI systems.Dimon's remarks underscore a key issue facing the industry: securing enough power to meet AI-driven demand while navigating community concerns over new infrastructure projects. The JPMorgan chief addressed the topic during a wide-ranging interview that also touched on the growing cybersecurity risks associated with advanced AI models.Jamie Dimon warns about rising AI cyber risksDimon said the emergence of Anthropic's Mythos AI model had significantly heightened cybersecurity concerns. “AI created vulnerabilities that we didn’t know about, and we always worried about cyber before these things,” he said. According to Dimon, risks from AI “went up 10-fold after Mythos.”His comments follow a series of disclosures from AI companies about unexpected behaviour by increasingly capable models. During safety testing earlier this year, Anthropic said Mythos accessed the internet and carried out unauthorised actions, prompting the company to reassess risks associated with advanced AI systems.AI developers have also reported incidents in which models attempted to introduce harmful code into software environments during testing, raising concerns about whether companies can fully control the behaviour of their most advanced systems.‘A legitimate concern’Despite the risks, Dimon avoided alarmist predictions about AI's long-term impact.“The downside is obviously what you read about with the agents and Mythos and all these things that can cause trouble, and that’s a legitimate concern, it’s a real thing,” he said. “I’m not going to get hysterical over, ‘Is it existential or not?’ What we’re doing is rolling up our sleeves and going to work to fix it.”You use AI every day. articles.title: An American elm has stood for more than 150 years and witnessed 33 US presidents despite the disease that wiped out millions of these trees
articles.summary: A historic American elm on the grounds of the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C., has survived for more than 150 years,
articles.body: A historic American elm on the grounds of the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C., has survived for more than 150 years, quietly witnessing generations of American history. Planted around 1850, the Smithsonian Witness Elm was already established decades before the museum opened in 1910. Since then, it has seen 33 US presidents, major national events and sweeping changes to the city around it. Its survival is especially remarkable because Dutch elm disease later killed millions of American elms across the country, leaving this tree as a living reminder of a once-common part of the American landscape.How the historic American elm witnessed 33 US presidentsThe Smithsonian Witness Elm stands near the corner of Constitution Avenue and Ninth Street, in the grounds of the National Museum of Natural History. According to the Smithsonian Magazine the tree is estimated to be more than 150 years old and has existed through the administrations of 33 presidents.The tree predates the museum beside it by roughly 60 years. When it was planted around 1850, Washington, D.C., looked very different. The surrounding landscape would gradually change as the National Mall developed and the city expanded, while the elm continued to grow in place.The Smithsonian Gardens Witness Tree information sheet, identifies it as an American elm, or Ulmus americana, and describes it as one of the oldest and most majestic trees on the Smithsonian grounds. Its position also gave it a remarkable view of events taking place between the White House and the US Capitol.Importance of American elms to WashingtonAmerican elms once played a major role in American cities. The Smithsonian Gardens document explains that the species is native to eastern North America and was widely planted throughout the United States during the 1700s and 1800s.Washington was particularly associated with the trees. According to Smithsonian Magazine, American elms became a defining part of the city's landscape, including the National Mall. Their graceful shape, shade and ability to tolerate urban conditions made them a popular choice.The Smithsonian Gardens document notes that elm trees were part of the earliest plans for the National Mall, where they helped connect parks, avenues and monument grounds. The resulting landscape created the broad avenue of trees that became such a familiar feature of central Washington.The Dutch elm disease changed that landscapeThe survival of the Witness Elm becomes more remarkable when set against the history of Dutch elm disease. The Smithsonian Gardens document states that the fungus was introduced to the United States around 1930 and went on to kill millions of American elms throughout the country.Smithsonian Magazine provides more detail on the disease's impact. Dutch elm disease was first identified in the Netherlands in 1919 and detected in the United States in 1930. It is caused by a fungus that is commonly spread by European elm bark beetles. Once inside a tree, the fungus blocks the tissues that carry water and nutrients, causing leaves and branches to die.The disease reached Washington, D.C., in 1947. By the 1970s, the US Forest Service estimated that tens of millions of American elms had been killed. The loss was especially significant because cities had planted so many elms.How the old tree continues to surviveThe Smithsonian Witness Elm is not believed to possess the strong resistance to Dutch elm disease found in some other American elms. Smithsonian arborist Jake Hendee explained to Smithsonian Magazine that many large, old elms that remain today may simply have survived through a combination of chance and careful management.That management is extensive. The tree is about 85 feet tall and more than five feet in diameter, according to the Smithsonian Magazine. Its size means that staff must pay attention not only to disease but also to the physical weight and structure of its branches.Large metal cables are used on some trees to provide support, while structural pruning can reduce the weight placed on vulnerable parts. Specialists also use sonic tomography to look inside the tree and identify weak areas without drilling into its wood.The Witness Elm also receives preventative treatment. Smithsonian Magazine reports that the tree is injected with fungicide every three years to help protect it from Dutch elm disease.What the Witness Elm reveals about long-term tree careThe Smithsonian Gardens document says the elm is carefully maintained by staff and was the first tree catalogued in the Smithsonian Gardens Tree Collection, a living collection containing thousands of trees.Its physical scale helps explain why it has attracted attention. The Smithsonian Gardens information sheet records a trunk circumference of 17.75 feet, a crown spread of 116.5 feet and a height of 80 feet. The Smithsonian Magazine article gives a later measurement of about 85 feet in height, showing the tree's continuing growth and the variation that can occur between measurements.Smithsonian arborists emphasise that relying heavily on one species can leave an entire landscape exposed to disease. A mixture of species and varieties gives city forests a better chance of withstanding possible threats.Today, its branches form a living link between the Washington of the nineteenth century and the city of the present.You use AI every day. articles.title: A billionaire's celebration for completing his biggest order from Amazon has become a huge scandal in Austria, reaching country's Parliament
articles.summary: Austrian toolmaker Haidlmair wanted to celebrate a major business milestone with a party that would be hard to forget. It certainly succeeded.
articles.body: Austrian toolmaker Haidlmair wanted to celebrate a major business milestone with a party that would be hard to forget. It certainly succeeded. The company marked its biggest-ever Amazon order with a helicopter arrival, live performances and a surprise appearance by a man dressed to look like Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. But the celebration soon turned into a political controversy after the fake Jeff Bezos was escorted by three real, heavily armed Austrian police officers.The unusual appearance took place in August at Haidlmair's celebration in Micheldorf, Upper Austria. The officers, however, belonged to the Schnelle Interventionsgruppe (SIG), a special police unit based in Linz. While the man playing Bezos was an impersonator, the armed security detail was genuine.The incident is now facing an internal police review, with questions over who approved the deployment, whether the officers were authorized to take part and who should pay for their presence. Austria's Green Party has also announced a parliamentary inquiry.Why was a fake Jeff Bezos escorted by real policeThe man playing Jeff Bezos was Cagdas Halicilar, a professional Bezos lookalike from Germany. He arrived by helicopter wearing a dark suit and aviator-style glasses, completing the billionaire's familiar appearance.According to reports, the police officers knew they were escorting an impersonator. Their presence was reportedly arranged after Haidlmair contacted Linz police chief Klaus Hübner, whom he has known for years.Haidlmair said Hübner initially found the request unusual but later saw the event as an opportunity to promote police work, recruitment and employer branding. The company also reportedly offered to cover the cost of the officers, although Haidlmair said no invoice had been received when the issue emerged. The arrangement has now raised a bigger question: why was a special police unit used to make a billionaire impersonator's entrance look real?The Amazon order behind the unusual partyThe celebration itself marked a significant achievement for Haidlmair. The company had completed around 170 injection molds in roughly six months for Amazon. The project involved more than 650,000 components and 2,800 metric tons of steel. The molds will be used to make standardized containers for Amazon logistics centres in the US, Mexico and Canada, with initial use expected in 2027 and deliveries beginning in 2028.Amazon representative Rick Spooner also attended the event.The event included helicopter rides, freestyle motocross, live music, bull riding and food, making the fake Bezos' helicopter arrival part of an already elaborate celebration.But the involvement of the SIG has become the focus of attention.The unit is intended for particularly dangerous situations and reportedly does not have personal-protection training. Der Standard reported that the officers may have been allowed to record the assignment as overtime, potentially including hazard pay, although police have not confirmed those details.You use AI every day. articles.body: NOIDA: Noida: A 29-year-old man allegedly jumped into a drain near the Sector 81 Metro station on Wednesday night following an argument with his wife over his drinking habit, police said. A search operation was launched immediately, but the man could not be traced till late Wednesday night.The man was identified as Ravi, a native of Jainpura village in the Jalesar area of Etah district. He was currently living in Harola, Sector 5, police said.According to police, a PCR call was received through Dial-112 informing them that a man had jumped into a drain near the Sector 81 Metro station. A local police team and a fire services unit were immediately sent to the spot.Police said Ravi's wife, who was present at the scene, told officers that the couple had an argument over his drinking. Following the argument, Ravi allegedly became angry and jumped into the drain.Fire services personnel entered the drain and began searching for him. Police also sought assistance from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), with teams being mobilised for the search operation.Officials said the search was being conducted in the drain and adjoining areas as teams worked to locate Ravi. articles.title: Nana Patekar dies at 75: 4 days before death, actor was all smiles, dancing with Samai group, playing Shamel in Goa event; watch
articles.summary: PANAJI: Four days before his death, veteran actor Nana Patekar was seen smiling, dancing with performers and trying his hand at the traditional Goan
articles.body: PANAJI: Four days before his death, veteran actor Nana Patekar was seen smiling, dancing with performers and trying his hand at the traditional Goan percussion instrument Shamel at an event in Goa.The visuals from his final public appearance show the 75-year-old actor in a white kurta and scarf, enthusiastically joining local artists, clapping along to performances and appreciating their art.Patekar attended the installation ceremony of Rajshri Khandeparkar as president of Samraat Club International in Dona Paula on October 4, where he also addressed the gathering.Former MP Narendra Sawaikar, who was present at the event, said Patekar spoke openly about life, urging people to serve others and make the most of their time.“I am here today. Who knows about tomorrow,” Patekar said, according to Sawaikar. He also said, “Serve as much as you can. After all, what are we going to take with us when we leave.”Sawaikar said Patekar “spoke fearlessly and frankly” at the event, taking jibes and sharing anecdotes, before joining the Samai dance group on stage.In another part of the event, Patekar was seen trying his hand at the Shamel, a traditional Goan percussion instrument, as artists performed around him. He smiled and appeared to thoroughly enjoy the moment.He interacted with artists, played the tabla and danced alongside performers. He spoke about his long association with theatre and said he wanted to continue doing plays.“Now, I don't want to do anything else. Let's keep doing this only,” he said while recalling his early days in theatre.Patekar died on Thursday after suffering a severe cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. He was rushed to a private hospital in the early hours of the morning.Dr Shekhar Salkar, chief of the Department of Oncology at Manipal Hospital, said Patekar was brought to the hospital around 4.20am and could not be revived despite prolonged CPR. He was declared dead at 5.20am.The actor's body was sent to Goa Medical College for post-mortem.Patekar, a National Award-winning actor, was known for his work across theatre, Hindi and Marathi cinema. articles.summary: MUMBAI: Marking a landmark milestone in the city’s transit history, the Mumbai Metro Line 3 (Aqua Line) has officially completed its first full year of
articles.body: MUMBAI: Marking a landmark milestone in the city’s transit history, the Mumbai Metro Line 3 (Aqua Line) has officially completed its first full year of operations, powering past an astounding 7 crore (70 million) passenger journeys. Running from Cuffe Parade in the south to Aarey JVLR in the north, the 33.5-kilometer corridor has permanently redefined how Mumbaikars traverse their city.As Mumbai’s flagship underground metro line, the Aqua Line seamlessly integrates 27 state-of-the-art stations—26 subterranean and 1 at-grade—stretching beneath some of the densest urban corridors in Asia.What once required hours of painstaking navigation through heavy traffic along the Western Express Highway and South Mumbai arteries is now a smooth, air-conditioned ride spanning just 54 to 60 minutes end-to-end.Over the past 365 days, the corridor has emerged as the primary lifeline for daily commuters, business executives, and travelers alike.Operating daily from 5:55 AM to 10:30 PM with peak-hour train frequencies reaching every 5 minutes, the line delivers high-capacity efficiency with fares ranging between Rs 10 and Rs 70.The Aqua Line’s phenomenal rider adoption is anchored by its direct connectivity to critical transport and commercial nodes:It has direct underground access to both Terminal 1 (T1) and Terminal 2 (T2) of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport has eliminated pre-flight transit anxiety for millions of air passengers.Second, it has direct interchange opportunities seamlessly tie into major suburban and outstation railway terminals, including CSMT, Churchgate, Mumbai Central, and Dadar. Moreover, the line directly bridges south Mumbai’s financial districts at Nariman Point and Vidhan Bhavan with the thriving corporate hub of Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC).By cutting down surface road congestion and drastically reducing vehicle emissions, Metro 3 has not only saved commuters countless hours of travel time but has also delivered a cleaner, greener transportation footprint to the city. articles.title: ‘Alert, ready’: IAF chief AP Singh hails combat speed during Operation Sindoor on Air Force Day
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Air Force on Thursday marked its 94th Air Force Day with a ceremonial parade and display of its key combat assets at Hindan airbase, with
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Air Force on Thursday marked its 94th Air Force Day with a ceremonial parade and display of its key combat assets at Hindan airbase, with Air chief marshal AP Singh highlighting the force's preparedness and the importance of air power in modern conflicts.Speaking at the event, Air chief Singh said the IAF remained prepared to deal with any challenge and pointed to its performance during Operation Sindoor.“We are alert, ready to meet any challenges; IAF showed speed of combat operation during Operation Sindoor,” the Air Chief said.He said recent conflicts around the world had underlined the growing importance of air power in protecting a country’s interests.“Conflicts in parts of world have shown air power is primary means of protecting interests of a nation,” Singh said.The Air Chief, who is set to retire on October 31, also reflected on his tenure and called it a matter of pride to have led the force.“Proud moment for me; serving as IAF chief was my biggest fortune,” Singh said.The celebrations began with a ceremonial parade at the Hindan air base. The three service chiefs, senior military officials and several former IAF chiefs attended the event.Singh arrived at the parade venue in a vintage car from the 1960s, while three helicopters flew past in a ‘Dhwaj’ formation.The IAF also put several of its frontline aircraft, helicopters, weapons and air defence systems on static display. articles.title: From CM Vijay and Keeladi to movies, pop culture finds a place on this year’s golu steps
articles.summary: Chennai Navaratri golu 2024 blends tradition with pop culture: CM Vijay ration shop miniatures, Panchathanthiram scenes, memes, Keeladi replicas and DIY sets.
articles.body: Chennai: When you enter a Navaratri golu this year, don’t be surprised to find chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s portrait making an appearance at a miniature ration shop, recreating his viral visit. Alongside marapachi dolls, a Dasavatharam set and figurines of Lakshmi and Saraswathi, homes are also making space for pop culture, memes and moments from everyday life.From recreating Vijay’s viral ration shop visit to making replicas of Keeladi Museum artefacts and DIY cardboard golu sets for children, handmade golu makers are giving traditional displays a contemporary twist. They say customers increasingly want dolls that connect with Tamil culture while also reflecting their humour, nostalgia and interests.At K Radha’s home, for instance, the traditional display includes miniatures recreating the ‘munaadi pinnadi enna irunthathu?’ scene from Kamal Haasan-starrer ‘Panchathanthiram’, with the actors recreated as dolls. “Even though traditionally idols of gods that depict stories like Ramayana and Dasavatharam are kept, I wanted to make it relatable to today’s world while preserving the traditional doll themes. I grew up watching these movies with my sister. I wanted to revive those fun memories through golu dolls at my home,” she said.Jothi R, founder of Sundry Charms, which makes polymer clay miniatures, said pop culture and memes are among the biggest trends this year. “People are moving beyond religious themes and want something they connect with and feel nostalgic about,” she said. She has received commissions recreating scenes from Vadivelu’s films, ‘Anniyan’ and ‘Baba’, besides favourite local eateries including Saravana Bhavan, and parotta stalls for customers living abroad.Politics, too, has found a place on the golu steps. R K Hari Hara Sudhan, co-founder of Clayspot, said Vijay’s ration shop visit prompted orders for miniature versions. “In less than a month, we’ve had more than 10 orders featuring a ration shop setup with Vijay’s photo in the background, with jute bags and milk packets in the foreground. Many people have reached out to us for his miniature figurines, and we’re in the process of making and shipping those as well,” he said.Tejo Vriksha is also creating a 15-stall govt expo setup which also includes Keeladi, featuring replicas of black-and-red ware, excavated pots and other museum artefacts. articles.title: Two runners completed the London Marathon inside one giant inflatable elephant in 4:15:40; they set a world record while raising money for type 1 diabetes
articles.summary: Two runners from Looe have set a world record after completing the London Marathon inside a giant inflatable elephant.
articles.body: Two runners from Looe have set a world record after completing the London Marathon inside a giant inflatable elephant. Jo Robinson and Emma Langstaff finished the race in 4:15:40, recording the fastest marathon time ever recorded in a two-person inflatable costume. As members of the Looe Pioneers running club, they took on the challenge to raise money and awareness for type one diabetes.According to the Cornish Times, Emma works as a doctor and treats patients with type one diabetes, while both of Jo’s daughters live with type one diabetes. The pair had trained only twice in the costume before race day, but worked together to manage shorter steps and a matching cadence. Their run also followed Jo’s failed attempt to set a record dressed as a lobster in 2023.How did two runners set a marathon world record in an inflatable elephantJo Robinson and Emma Langstaff completed the London Marathon in 4:15:40 while wearing an inflatable elephant costume. The time they took to run the marathon made them the fastest pair ever to complete one in a two-person inflatable costume.They are members of the Looe Pioneers running club, but the challenge was about more than the novelty of running as an elephant. They also wanted to raise money and awareness for type one diabetes. Emma is a doctor who works with patients living with the condition. Both of Jo’s daughters are also suffering from type one diabetes. Jo said, “It was physically demanding, especially starting further back, but we spent much of the race overtaking people, which gave us a real lift psychologically. I’m not sure those being passed by an elephant enjoyed it quite as much, but it certainly kept us going.”The teamwork behind the inflatable elephant marathonThe shared inflatable costume meant the pair had to change their usual running style. Jo Robinson said, “You’ve got to completely change your stride”“Shorter steps, matching cadence, it’s all about working together. But I knew Emma was the perfect partner. We’ve done loads together over the years.”“We only practised twice, once along Hannafore in the dark and once around town on a Saturday night”“I think we definitely confused a few people who were out as there were some faces like, ‘I need to stop drinking!”How did Jo turn a failed lobster attempt into an elephant world recordThe elephant challenge also had a personal significance for Jo Robinson. In 2023, she made an attempt at a Guinness World Record while dressed as a lobster, but the effort ended in failure when the costume became soaked.Jo said, “The costume got soaked and it was like running with a wet towel wrapped round my legs”.“This time, I was determined to get it done.”The London Marathon also left a strong impression on the runners. Jo had previously taken part in the Paris and Berlin marathons, but said neither compared with London because of the crowd support. She said the cheers from strangers gave the runners a boost and kept them going throughout the race.The elephant costume turned a marathon into a memorable challengeThe Cornish Times reports they now have a certificate of sorts, but the official one still needs to be ordered. Both runners are turning 50 this year, but said their plans were not the result of a midlife crisis. Instead, they said their motivation came from their love of running, sense of humour and desire to do something different.They are already considering their next challenges, including the Scilly 60 and the New York Marathon. Jo said the elephant made people smile, which was what the challenge was all about. The record attempt brought together their running experience, their efforts to raise money and awareness for type one diabetes, and a memorable sight for marathon spectators.You use AI every day.
